Serve an external app process with a command

Source: R/serve.R
pz_serve_command.Rd

Starts any local server command – a Shiny for Python app (shiny run app.py), a dev server, anything that binds a port – in a background process and returns a handle for its lifecycle. Pass the handle to pz_open() to open pages on the server; closing those pages leaves it running.

Usage

pz_serve_command(
  command,
  args = character(),
  ...,
  wd = NULL,
  port = NULL,
  envvars = NULL,
  path = "/",
  wait = c("load", "shiny"),
  timeout = 10
)

Arguments

command

The command to run, found on PATH or given as a path.

args

Character vector of arguments. The string {port} in any argument is replaced with the port the server should listen on.

...

Reserved; must be empty.

wd

Working directory for the command; defaults to the current directory.

port

The port to listen on. NULL (the default) picks a random free port; if startup fails because the port was taken, a new port is tried. When port is NULL, {port} must appear in args or envvars so the command learns the chosen port. Pass a number when the command fixes its own port: paparazzi skips picking but still checks the port is free before starting and waits for it to listen.

envvars

Named character vector of environment variables set in the process, on top of the inherited environment; {port} is replaced here too. NULL adds no environment overrides.

path

URL path the app responds at. The handle's $url is http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>.

wait

What pz_open() with wait = "auto" waits for on pages opened from this handle: "shiny" waits for Shiny idle (the case for Shiny for Python apps), "load" (the default) waits for the page to load.

timeout

Seconds to wait for the command to start listening; defaults to 10.

Value

A PaparazziServe handle with public fields url and port and methods stop(), logs(), and is_running().

Details

The handle has the same contract as pz_serve_shiny(): $stop() interrupts, waits, then kills the process tree, and is idempotent, so withr::defer(server$stop()) is a safe cleanup. A finalizer stops the process as a last resort. Standard output and errors go to a temporary log file (never an undrained pipe), readable mid-run with $logs().

Examples

# Any command that binds a port works; {port} is replaced with the
# port paparazzi picks
server <- pz_serve_command(
  file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
  c(
    "-e",
    "httpuv::runServer('127.0.0.1', {port}, list(call = function(req) list(status = 200L, body = 'served by a command')))"
  )
)
page <- pz_open(server)
pz_get_text(page, target = "body")
#> [1] "served by a command"
pz_close(page)
server$stop()
